description.narrative: The expected impact of the project will be improved living conditions in urban areas. The outcome will be improved infrastructure and access to service delivery in poor urban neighborhoods in 20 project cities. The Project will have three outputs: (i) Institutional capacities for managing pro-poor urban development are strengthened; (ii) Infrastructure investment plans to upgrade poor neighborhoods are aligned with the overall city development plans and implemented; and (iii) Public private partnerships are established to promote new settlements for poor families.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Improved infrastructure and access to service delivery in poor urban neighborhoods in project cities

At least 50% of community members in project locations, of which half are women, are satisfied with improvements in roads, provision of drinking water, sanitation facilities, and other basic urban infrastructure [Baseline: 0%; perception survey will be conducted by 2017] Achievement: 99.1 Progress/Status: 99.1% community members in project locations were satisfied with improvements in roads, provision of drinking water, sanitation facilities, and other basic infrastructures. Women were 90.0% satisfied with the improvement of the facilities and infrastructures. Data Source: PPMS reports Consultant reports District and city administration evaluation reports
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Infrastructure investment plans to upgrade poor neighborhoods are aligned with the overall city development plans and implemented Indicator: 268,000 households benefit from upgraded sanitation facilities/systems Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Achieved. The upgraded sanitation facilities and systems, which include the drainage system benefitted 311,849 households. Data Source: PPMS reports Consultant reports District and city administration

Output: Infrastructure investment plans to upgrade poor neighborhoods are aligned with the overall city development plans and implemented Indicator: 50,000 households benefit from upgraded water supply facilities/systems Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Achieved. The upgraded water supply facilities and systems benefitted 105,371. Data Source: PPMS reports Consultant reports District and city administration

Output: Infrastructure investment plans to upgrade poor neighborhoods are aligned with the overall city development plans and implemented Indicator: 500 km of neighborhood roads are upgraded Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Achieved. The project upgraded 770.69 km neighborhood roads in 209 neighborhoods. Data Source: PPMS reports Consultant reports District and city administration

Output: Infrastructure investment plans to upgrade poor neighborhoods are aligned with the overall city development plans and implemented Indicator: Community implementation organizations (CIOs/BKMs) in all project neighborhoods are functioning with 40% representation of women in each CIO/BKM Achievement: 92 Progress/Status: Partially Achieved. The project established functioning BKM in project neighborhoods with 33.2% representation of women involved in the decision-making meetings. Data Source: PPMS reports Consultant reports District and city administration

Output: Infrastructure investment plans to upgrade poor neighborhoods are aligned with the overall city development plans and implemented Indicator: Individual NUPs of the project neighborhoods are integrated in the consolidated city infrastructure upgrading investment plan and harmonized with approved RTRW and SPPIP. ) Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: Achieved. The project reviewed 209 NUAPs in 2017 and compiled 215 CAPs in 99 subdistricts in 2018 based on the reviewed NUAP. The project compiled 61 CAPs in 31 subdistricts in 2019 based on NUAPs that had been reviewed in 2019. Data Source: PPMS reports Consultant reports District and city administration evaluation reports Feedback from communities

Output: Infrastructure investment plans to upgrade poor neighborhoods are aligned with the overall city development plans and implemented Indicator: More than 80% of infrastructure works are evaluated as being of in accordance with the standard and have functioning O&M arrangements. Achievement: 75 Progress/Status: Partially Achieved. 97.76% infrastructures were in accordance with the national standard. MPWH approved the handover of 38 infrastructures in 2020. DGHS in February 2021 requested 14 provincial governments to expedite the process and Semarang and Pekalongan cities responded to proceed. Other 22 infrastructures are being verified and the documents for the remaining 6 infrastructures are being collected. Data Source: PPMS reports Consultant reports District and city administration

Output: Institutional capacities for managing pro-poor urban development in an environmentally and socially sustainable manner are strengthened Indicator: At least 100 local government staff (30% women) dealing with spatial planning trained on CDD approaches adopted in urban development; and environmental subjects related to water treatment, sanitation, solid waste management, project management, O&M, and other areas identified in the capacity needs assessments Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Achieved. 561 local government staff have participated in the training, short course, and Master's degree program with 176 (31%) of the participants are women. Data Source: PPMS reports Consultant reports District and city administration evaluation reports

Output: Institutional capacities for managing pro-poor urban development in an environmentally and socially sustainable manner are strengthened Indicator: Local government officials involved in developing and/or revising integrated urban development plans and SIAPs adopt community-driven development approaches by 2017 Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Achieved. All participating cities/districts have prepared and legalized SIAPs through Mayor Regulation. SIAPs become the reference for the implementation of slum alleviation program at cities/ districts level, including NUSP2 and other similar programs. Data Source: PPMS reports Consultant reports District and city administration evaluation reports

Output: New Settlements for poor families established. Indicator: Affordable housing rental schemes are adopted in at least four cities in which local governments shall introduce regulations on the management of the new settlement sites, including residential tenancy scheme. Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Partially achieved. • The affordable housing rental scheme had been introduced in all NSD locations. Beneficiaries who occupied the NSD houses in Kendari, Palopo, Bima, and Kapuas signed rental agreement in which included the tenancy provision. • Mayor Decree on the NSD implementation arrangements had been issued in all NSD cities. Rental rate has been set in Kapuas, Bima, and Palopo through Mayor Decree while in Kendari the tariff was provided in the rental agreement but not yet established through Mayor Decree. Data Source: District and city administration evaluation reports

Output: New Settlements for poor families established. Indicator: At least 800 poor families (priority to households headed by women) living in slums and disaster prone areas are provided houses under affordable housing rental scheme in new housing areas. Achievement: 501 Progress/Status: Partially Achieved • 650 houses were constructed of which 501 houses were occupied. The government of Bima starts the construction of 20 units in 2021 and requested budget for 58 units in 2022. In Bima, 5 houses are retained as empty to government commitment for disaster emergency response, while 165 units in Kapuas are empty as the units are being used as COVID-19 quarantine facility. Rental payment has been collected in May 2019 in Palopo and in August 2019 in Bima. Rental payment has not been collected in Kendari as the government focused on the establishment of NSD management and occupancy administration. Moreover, the rental payment cannot be collected in Kapuas as the government wait until the Regent Decree in 2020 is lifted. Data Source: District and city administration evaluation reports

Output: New Settlements for poor families established. Indicator: New housing areas for poor families are constructed in at least 4 cities. Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Achieved. The NSD has been implemented in Kendari city, Bima city, Palopo city, and Kapuas district. Data Source: PPMS reports Consultant reports
